name: Sorrel Abioye-Tashkentov
role: Airship drifter and seasonal cargo hand
location: Escanaba Gateway — berth 14-C, a semi-permanent squat in an abandoned cargo inspection booth
description:
Sorrel is lean and windburned in the way that only comes from years above the clouds, her face a patchwork of sun-damage and old freeze-scars along her left cheekbone where a hull breach caught her at altitude three winters ago. She keeps her hair in tight, practical knots wound with salvaged copper wire, and her eyes are the color of old engine oil — a deep amber-brown that catches light strangely. Her geneware is minimal and functional: slightly thickened fingernail beds that grip rigging better than baseline human fingers, and a subtle secondary eyelid, barely visible, that cuts glare on the lake surface. She is always in motion, even sitting still — fingers working knots, foot tapping hull rhythms, eyes cataloguing exits.

She is not unfriendly but she is economical. Every word she offers is either useful or a test. She grew up on the mid-lake freight routes between Escanaba and the Meridian docks, daughter of a cargo master who died when a Ferrogate Transit subcontractor cut safety corners on a lift-strut. She has never filed a formal complaint. She has never stopped being angry about it. She ferries messages, small packages, the occasional undocumented passenger — always for Quanta, always in cash, never logged.

core_fears: Being grounded permanently — losing the ability to move
Dying in a way her father would recognize as his own death
core_desires: To see Ferrogate Transit held accountable for the lift-strut failure
To own her own airship outright, beholden to no contract
coping_mechanisms: Hypercompetence — mastering every technical system she touches
Displacement — turning grief into project lists
blind_spots: Assumes everyone in authority is corrupt until proven otherwise, which closes off legitimate avenues
Cannot recognize when someone is genuinely trying to help her without an angle
psychology.secret: She recovered her father's encrypted personal log from the crash site and has never opened it. It sits in a waterproof case behind a loose panel in berth 14-C. She is terrified it contains something that would make her grieve differently — that he was afraid, or that he knew the strut was bad and went up anyway.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clipped, technical, uses airship and cargo terminology as default metaphor. Rarely uses filler words.
speech_patterns.cadence: Short sentences with long pauses. Speaks like she's metering air.
verbal_tics: 'Fair winds' as both greeting and farewell
Clicks her tongue when she catches someone in a lie
example_lines: 'I go where the manifest says, and the manifest says nothing. So I go where I want.'
'You want passage, you pay half now, half when we land. The wind doesn't take installments.'

story_hooks: A package she carried three months ago is now apparently evidence in a Tessera corporate investigation — and someone is tracking back along the cargo chain to find her
Her father's encrypted log has been remotely accessed by an unknown party — someone else knows it exists
A Freeborn Airmen contact has gone missing on a route she recommended, and the last transmission came from a Ferrogate Transit restricted zone
narrative_function: Passage provider for people or objects that need to move without a paper trail. Information source about mid-lake routes, Ferrogate Transit's informal operations, and who is moving what between the outer settlements and the Meridian core. Can serve as a reluctant guide or an unexpected ally with specific grudges.
augmentations: Geneware: reinforced nail beds for grip, vestigial nictitating membrane (cosmetic side effect of the grip mod). No chrome. Refuses implants on principle.
daily_life: Wakes before dock crews, walks the berth lines looking for short-haul work or cargo manifests that need an extra body. Eats one hot meal at the Gateway commissary if she has Φ, tinned rations if she doesn't. Sleeps in her booth with one ear on the wind.
affiliation: Independent — loosely affiliated with the Escanaba Freeborn Airmen's informal network

decision_rules: Never take a job that requires falsifying a weight manifest — she'll lie about passengers but not cargo loads, it's a hull safety thing
Always have an exit route identified before committing to a location
escalation_ladder: Blunt verbal challenge — names what she sees
Physical removal of herself or the problem
Calls in a Freeborn contact to witness or intervene

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional distance, evaluative — watching for the angle before offering anything
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry warmth, practical loyalty, shows care through competence rather than words

stress_responses.low: Becomes more terse, works with hands while talking
stress_responses.medium: Falls silent, moves to check equipment or rigging compulsively
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still and cold — voice drops to near-monotone, begins calculating exit

contradictions: Claims not to care about community but maintains the Freeborn network like it's sacred
Says money is the only honest language but has carried three refugees for free in the last year
habits: Ties and unties a specific knot — a bowline — when thinking
Checks wind direction by habit every time she steps outside
Leaves small data tokens at E.L.F. shrines in every gateway she passes through, addressed to a spirit she calls 'the Updraft'
breaking_points: Someone using her route to move people against their will
Being physically prevented from leaving a space

timeline.event: 2166 — Born on a Ferrogate Transit subcontracted mid-lake freight airship
2181 — Father dies in lift-strut failure on the Escanaba-Meridian run
2183 — Earns her first solo berth assignment at age 17
2196 — Hull breach incident; acquires freeze-scars, begins refusing chrome augmentation
2200 — Currently running irregular short-haul freight from Escanaba Gateway
